hypothesis: the six provider/cost defects in the 2026-07-26 review (5 fallback spend unreported, 6 pricing crash after billing, 7 empty/truncated responses billed silently, 18 Anthropic never raises ContentPolicyError, 19 bare 'o' prefix, 20 empty memo re-billed) can be fixed offline at EUR0
result: landed as A4 (merge e52930a) AFTER ONE BOUNCE. 379 passed on the fully merged tree (A1+A2+A4), black+ruff clean, EUR0. Hash gate re-run: all six books unchanged. Non-invalidation re-run: 13426/13426 byte-identical and resolving. THE BOUNCE IS THE FINDING: the first implementation made providers raise instead of returning '' and thereby broke the retry ladder, which catches only ValueError (:476,:487) and ContentPolicyError (:414,:566) while the raises happen inside client.complete() at :472/:483, outside every handler. A truncation went from 'degrade to per-segment fallback' to 'abort mid-book' — strictly worse, because per-segment retry IS the right remedy for a truncation (one segment per call is a far smaller prompt) and the cache commits per batch, so a resume rebuilt the same oversized prompt and aborted again. Found by Supervisor inspection; no reviewer agent produced a verdict all session. The landed version degrades at all four sites with a smaller unit (batch rung, revise pass, book-context memo) and stays loud at _translate_single, which has none; truncated calls carry their already-billed CompletionResult so cost still reaches stats.cost_eur. Finding 18 corrects the review: Anthropic signals refusals BOTH as BadRequestError and in-band via stop_reason='refusal' (SDK-typed in anthropic==0.109.1), so the prescribed BadRequestError wrapper misses the in-band case.

hypothesis: the Kotlin LLM client can be hardened against review findings 6, 7 and 18 by porting the CORRECTED Python algorithm rather than today's, giving the on-device translate engine (B5) a failure shape it can degrade on instead of one it must undo
result: landed as B6 (first Kotlin story of m4). 580 JVM tests (314 debug incl. 26 skipped screenshot + 266 release), 0 failures, up from a 536 baseline; Android Lint clean on touched files; EUR0. Finding 6: requireKnownModel pre-flights inside createLlmClient before either client is constructed, so nothing reaches costEur post-billing. Finding 7: EMPTY_COMPLETION/TRUNCATED_COMPLETION carry the already-billed LlmResult, mirroring the corrected Python shape — explicitly informed by A4's bounce, where making the failure loud removed the recovery handling it. Finding 18: Kotlin had NO content-policy signal; both the HTTP 400 body and Anthropic's in-band stop_reason='refusal' now raise it. Backoff went from one fixed 1000ms retry to up to 5 with base*2^(n-1)+jitter honouring Retry-After — one retry is thin for a ~162-call on-device book. All four guards mutation-proven live. SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED: the sole-construction-route claim is FALSE in Kotlin — SettingsViewModel.kt:60-61 builds both clients directly for the key-test feature, so unlike Python's create_client the finding-6 fix is not airtight; harmless today only because those models are hardcoded constants always in the pricing table. Filed to B7. Also confirmed error messages interpolate only a provider label and HTTP code, never a response body.
